scr_cash_deposits_register_report_column.purpose: Defines the Deposits Register columns — bank, deposit date, deposit number, receipts included, amount and cleared status — used to match deposits to bank credits.
scr_cash_deposits_register_report_column.outcome: Preparers can tell which deposits have cleared and which are still in transit.
scr_cash_deposits_register_report_column.rootCause: The cleared status and date columns identify deposits in transit at month-end, which must clear in the first days of the next month or be investigated.
scr_cash_deposits_register_report_column.ifSkipped: Stale deposits in transit are carried without investigation, hiding possible misappropriation.
redFlags: Deposits in transit older than five business days

scr_cash_receipts_register_report.purpose: Lists receipts recorded in Accounts Receivable — customer, date, method, amount and the invoices each receipt was applied to — with navigation to the underlying invoices.
scr_cash_receipts_register_report.outcome: A cash receipts register tying collections to invoices and deposits.
scr_cash_receipts_register_report.rootCause: Receipts must be traceable from customer to invoice to deposit; the register is the evidence chain used in audits of cash receipts and in resolving customer disputes.
scr_cash_receipts_register_report.ifSkipped: Collections cannot be traced to deposits and customer disputes are harder to resolve.
redFlags: Receipts applied on account without invoices

scr_cash_customizing_and_running_the_rec.purpose: Chooses customers, dates, methods and properties and runs the Receipts Register report.
scr_cash_customizing_and_running_the_rec.outcome: A receipts register for the requested scope.
scr_cash_customizing_and_running_the_rec.rootCause: Receipts reviews are typically by property and month; filtering by method helps spot unusual cash receipts at sites.
scr_cash_customizing_and_running_the_rec.ifSkipped: Reviews of cash receipts by method are not possible.
redFlags: High volume of cash (currency) receipts at a site

scr_cash_receipts_register_report_column.purpose: Defines the Receipts Register columns — customer, receipt date, method, reference, amount and applied invoices.
scr_cash_receipts_register_report_column.outcome: Correct reading of receipts and their application.
scr_cash_receipts_register_report_column.rootCause: The applied-invoices column shows whether receipts were applied correctly, which drives aging accuracy and late-fee assessment.
scr_cash_receipts_register_report_column.ifSkipped: Misapplied receipts go unnoticed and customers are dunned for balances they paid.

scr_cash_credit_card_register_report.purpose: Lists charges, fees and payments recorded against company credit card accounts for a period.
scr_cash_credit_card_register_report.outcome: A card activity register for reconciliation to issuer statements and spend review.
scr_cash_credit_card_register_report.rootCause: Card spending bypasses POs; a register lets reviewers see all card activity and reconcile it to statements.
scr_cash_credit_card_register_report.ifSkipped: Card activity escapes review and reconciliation.

scr_cash_customizing_and_running_the_cre.purpose: Selects card accounts and the issuer's statement period and runs the Credit Card Register report to support the monthly card reconciliation.
scr_cash_customizing_and_running_the_cre.outcome: Card activity for exactly the statement period.
scr_cash_customizing_and_running_the_cre.rootCause: Issuer statement cycles often close mid-month (e.g., the 18th), not at month-end. Running the register for the calendar month instead of the statement cycle makes the reconciliation fail.
scr_cash_customizing_and_running_the_cre.ifSkipped: Register periods do not align with statements and reconciliations fail.
redFlags: Register period not matching statement cycle

scr_cash_credit_card_register_report_col.purpose: Defines the Credit Card Register columns — card, date, merchant, type (charge, fee, payment) and amount.
scr_cash_credit_card_register_report_col.rootCause: Separating charges, fees and payments is necessary to reconcile to the statement's sections.
scr_cash_credit_card_register_report_col.ifSkipped: Card reconciliations mix activity types and fail.

scr_cash_setting_up_cash_management.purpose: Section on setting up Cash Management — configuration (journals, undeposited funds, available cash fields), accounts, reconciliation rules, and the More menu (ACH, electronic payments, bank feeds, positive pay, check layouts, owner distributions, holdbacks).
scr_cash_setting_up_cash_management.outcome: A fully configured cash application aligned with the company's banks and controls.
scr_cash_setting_up_cash_management.rootCause: Every cash control (positive pay, bank feeds, reconciliation rules, ACH) depends on setup. Missed setup means the control silently does not operate.
scr_cash_setting_up_cash_management.ifSkipped: Controls like positive pay or bank feeds never operate for some accounts.
redFlags: Bank accounts without positive pay or feed configuration

scr_cash_configuration.purpose: The Configuration menu of Cash Management setup, where company-wide cash settings are maintained.
scr_cash_configuration.outcome: Company-wide cash behaviors are defined once.
scr_cash_configuration.rootCause: Settings such as posting journals and escheat accounts apply to every property; central configuration keeps them consistent.
scr_cash_configuration.ifSkipped: Cash postings vary between properties and journals.

scr_cash_configure_cash_management_page.purpose: The Configure page where the journal for cash postings, undeposited funds handling, escheatment account and available cash fields are set.
scr_cash_configure_cash_management_page.outcome: Cash transactions post to the intended journal and accounts.
scr_cash_configure_cash_management_page.rootCause: Posting cash activity to the correct journal makes it identifiable in the GL and reviewable separately from other activity.
scr_cash_configure_cash_management_page.ifSkipped: Cash activity is mixed into general journals, complicating review.
redFlags: Cash journal set to the general journal

scr_cash_configuring_cash_management.purpose: Procedure for configuring Cash Management, including creating fields for entering available cash information by location.
scr_cash_configuring_cash_management.outcome: Available cash inputs and cash posting settings are configured.
scr_cash_configuring_cash_management.rootCause: Owners' distribution policies differ; configurable fields capture property-specific holdback information.
scr_cash_configuring_cash_management.ifSkipped: Available cash cannot reflect property-specific requirements.

scr_cash_accounts.purpose: The Accounts section of Cash Management setup covering bank and credit card account master records.
scr_cash_accounts.outcome: Bank and card accounts set up with correct GL mapping and restrictions.
scr_cash_accounts.rootCause: Account master data determines where every cash transaction posts; setup errors affect all activity on the account.
scr_cash_accounts.ifSkipped: Transactions post to wrong GL accounts or entities.

scr_cash_reconciliation_rules.purpose: The Reconciliation Rules section of setup, where intelligent bank matching rules and rule sets are defined.
scr_cash_reconciliation_rules.outcome: Automatic matching logic configured for the portfolio's bank accounts.
scr_cash_reconciliation_rules.rootCause: Rules let offshore teams reconcile high volumes consistently; they must be designed carefully to avoid false matches.
scr_cash_reconciliation_rules.ifSkipped: Matching remains manual and slow, and recs across hundreds of accounts miss the close deadline.

scr_cash_intelligent_bank_matching_for_b.purpose: Explains intelligent bank matching — rules that match bank and book transactions on amount, date tolerance, check number, reference and description, including one-to-many matches.
scr_cash_intelligent_bank_matching_for_b.outcome: Users understand how auto-matching decides and when it may mismatch.
scr_cash_intelligent_bank_matching_for_b.rootCause: Auto-matching is only reliable if users understand its logic; misunderstood rules produce wrong matches that hide exceptions.
scr_cash_intelligent_bank_matching_for_b.ifSkipped: Rules are set up poorly and produce wrong matches.

scr_cash_default_rules_for_checks_and_de.purpose: Describes the default matching rules for checks (check number and amount) and deposits (amount and date) that apply before custom rules.
scr_cash_default_rules_for_checks_and_de.outcome: Routine checks and deposits match automatically.
scr_cash_default_rules_for_checks_and_de.rootCause: Checks and deposits are the bulk of activity; sensible defaults handle most of it without custom setup.
scr_cash_default_rules_for_checks_and_de.ifSkipped: Users create redundant or conflicting custom rules.
redFlags: Custom rules overriding defaults without reason

scr_cash_example_of_a_one_to_many_rule.purpose: Worked example of a one-to-many rule — one bank credit matched to several book deposits, as happens with remote deposit capture or card processor settlements.
scr_cash_example_of_a_one_to_many_rule.outcome: Users can build rules for batched bank credits.
scr_cash_example_of_a_one_to_many_rule.rootCause: Card processors and some banks settle several days of receipts in one credit; without one-to-many rules these always need manual matching.
scr_cash_example_of_a_one_to_many_rule.ifSkipped: Batched credits remain manual exceptions every month.

scr_cash_rule_set_list.purpose: Lists rule sets — ordered collections of matching rules — and which bank accounts each applies to.
scr_cash_rule_set_list.outcome: Each bank account uses the right set of matching rules.
scr_cash_rule_set_list.rootCause: Different account types (operating vs trust vs payroll) need different matching logic; rule sets assign logic per account.
scr_cash_rule_set_list.ifSkipped: Accounts use inappropriate rules and mismatch.
redFlags: Accounts with no rule set assigned

scr_cash_adding_a_rule_set.purpose: Creates a rule set, ordering rules (e.g., match checks by number first, then deposits by amount and date) and assigning it to bank accounts.
scr_cash_adding_a_rule_set.outcome: A prioritized matching sequence for the assigned accounts.
scr_cash_adding_a_rule_set.rootCause: Rule order matters: stricter rules should run first so loose rules do not grab items that a strict rule would match correctly.
scr_cash_adding_a_rule_set.ifSkipped: Loose rules run first and create wrong matches.
redFlags: Loose amount-only rules ordered before check-number rules

scr_cash_viewing_or_editing_a_rule_set.purpose: Reviews or changes a rule set's rules, their order, or the bank accounts assigned to it — for example adding a rule for a new rent-payment processor's settlement pattern.
scr_cash_viewing_or_editing_a_rule_set.outcome: Rule sets stay effective as banks and transaction patterns change.
scr_cash_viewing_or_editing_a_rule_set.rootCause: New payment channels (e.g., a new rent payment processor) change bank patterns; rule sets must be updated to keep matching accurate.
scr_cash_viewing_or_editing_a_rule_set.ifSkipped: Matching rates drop and manual work rises.

scr_cash_deleting_or_inactivating_a_rule.purpose: Deletes or inactivates a rule set that is no longer used — for example the set built for a bank the portfolio has left.
scr_cash_deleting_or_inactivating_a_rule.outcome: Obsolete matching logic stops affecting reconciliations.
scr_cash_deleting_or_inactivating_a_rule.rootCause: Obsolete rule sets that remain assigned to accounts can keep producing wrong matches after transaction patterns change, and the errors are invisible because matches look complete.
scr_cash_deleting_or_inactivating_a_rule.ifSkipped: Outdated rules continue to run and silently mis-match transactions.
redFlags: Inactivating a rule set still assigned to active accounts

scr_cash_rule_set_information_page.purpose: The rule set record page showing its rules, their order of evaluation and the bank accounts it is assigned to.
scr_cash_rule_set_information_page.outcome: A clear definition of matching logic per account group.
scr_cash_rule_set_information_page.rootCause: Reviewers need to see the full matching logic to trust auto-matched reconciliations; an approver signing off a rec with 900 auto-matches must know what rules produced them.
scr_cash_rule_set_information_page.ifSkipped: Auto-matching is trusted without understanding and rule weaknesses go unchallenged.

scr_cash_rule_list.purpose: Lists individual intelligent bank matching rules — conditions on amount, date range, reference and description — available to include in rule sets.
scr_cash_rule_list.outcome: A library of matching rules for the portfolio.
scr_cash_rule_list.rootCause: Rules are reusable across rule sets; a library avoids duplicate or conflicting rules.
scr_cash_rule_list.ifSkipped: Duplicate rules with slightly different logic proliferate.

scr_cash_adding_a_rule.purpose: Creates a matching rule with operators (equals, within range) on fields like amount, date and description — for example matching a lender's monthly auto-debit by description 'LOAN PMT'.
scr_cash_adding_a_rule.rootCause: Recurring bank items (loan debits, payroll funding, card settlements) are predictable; rules eliminate repetitive manual matching.
scr_cash_adding_a_rule.ifSkipped: Recurring items require manual matching every month.
redFlags: Description rules broad enough to catch unrelated debits

scr_cash_viewing_or_editing_a_rule.purpose: Reviews or changes one matching rule's conditions — fields, operators and tolerances — for example after a bank renames the description of its loan payment debits.
scr_cash_viewing_or_editing_a_rule.outcome: Rules stay accurate as bank descriptions and patterns change.
scr_cash_viewing_or_editing_a_rule.rootCause: Banks change transaction descriptions without notice; rules keyed to descriptions stop matching until updated.
scr_cash_viewing_or_editing_a_rule.ifSkipped: Rules stop working after bank changes and recurring items fall back to manual matching.

scr_cash_deleting_or_inactivating_a_rule.purpose: Deletes or inactivates a matching rule that is obsolete or producing wrong matches.
scr_cash_deleting_or_inactivating_a_rule.rootCause: A rule that mismatches silently degrades every reconciliation it touches; removing it restores accuracy.
scr_cash_deleting_or_inactivating_a_rule.ifSkipped: Wrong matches continue each month and hide real exceptions.
redFlags: Rules with high unmatch rates still active

scr_cash_rule_information_page.purpose: The rule record page where a matching rule's conditions, operators (equals, within range) and tolerances for amount and date are defined.
scr_cash_rule_information_page.outcome: A precise definition of one matching rule.
scr_cash_rule_information_page.rootCause: Precision in conditions determines whether the rule matches only what it should; a date tolerance of 10 days on amount-only matching will pair unrelated identical rent payments.
scr_cash_rule_information_page.ifSkipped: Imprecise rules cause false matches that hide real exceptions.
redFlags: Tolerance fields left at wide defaults

scr_cash_more.purpose: The More section of Cash Management setup covering ACH and electronic payment bank configurations, bank feeds, positive pay, check updates and layouts, owner distributions and holdbacks.
scr_cash_more.outcome: Access to the setup of payment, fraud and distribution controls.
scr_cash_more.rootCause: Payment and fraud controls (ACH, positive pay, check layouts with MICR) are configured here; they must be complete for every issuing account.
scr_cash_more.ifSkipped: Payment controls are missing for some accounts.
redFlags: Issuing accounts without positive pay configuration

scr_cash_ach_bank_configurations_list.purpose: Lists ACH bank configurations — the origination settings (company ID, immediate origin and destination, file format) that each bank requires for ACH payment files.
scr_cash_ach_bank_configurations_list.outcome: Each originating bank has correct ACH file settings.
scr_cash_ach_bank_configurations_list.rootCause: Banks reject ACH files with incorrect header information; configurations must match each bank's specifications.
scr_cash_ach_bank_configurations_list.ifSkipped: ACH files are rejected and vendors are not paid.
gaap: NACHA Operating Rules — file header requirements

scr_cash_ach_frequently_asked_questions.purpose: Answers common ACH questions — paying vendors by ACH, prenotes, returns, file timing and which accounts can originate.
scr_cash_ach_frequently_asked_questions.outcome: Users resolve routine ACH questions without escalation.
scr_cash_ach_frequently_asked_questions.rootCause: ACH rules (prenotes, return timeframes, same-day windows) are unfamiliar to many accountants, especially new offshore staff.
scr_cash_ach_frequently_asked_questions.ifSkipped: ACH mistakes (missing prenotes, late files) recur.
redFlags: Repeated ACH returns for the same reason

scr_cash_adding_an_ach_bank_configuratio.purpose: Adds a bank's ACH configuration so accounts at that bank can originate ACH payment files.
scr_cash_adding_an_ach_bank_configuratio.outcome: Vendors can be paid by ACH from accounts at a new bank.
scr_cash_adding_an_ach_bank_configuratio.rootCause: A new banking relationship (after refinancing or acquisition) needs ACH origination set up before electronic payments can be made.
scr_cash_adding_an_ach_bank_configuratio.ifSkipped: Accounts at the new bank cannot pay vendors electronically.
redFlags: Configurations not tested with a prenote or test file

scr_cash_editing_an_ach_bank_configurati.purpose: Edits an ACH bank configuration when the bank changes file specifications or company IDs.
scr_cash_editing_an_ach_bank_configurati.outcome: ACH files continue to be accepted after bank changes.
scr_cash_editing_an_ach_bank_configurati.rootCause: Bank mergers and system upgrades change ACH specs; outdated configurations cause file rejections.
scr_cash_editing_an_ach_bank_configurati.ifSkipped: File rejections and late vendor payments.

scr_cash_viewing_an_ach_bank_configurati.purpose: Views an ACH bank configuration's settings — company ID, immediate origin and destination, file format — to verify them or troubleshoot a rejected ACH file.
scr_cash_viewing_an_ach_bank_configurati.outcome: Settings can be checked against the bank's specification when a file is rejected.
scr_cash_viewing_an_ach_bank_configurati.rootCause: When a bank rejects an ACH file, comparing the configuration to the bank's current specification is the first diagnostic step; most rejections trace to a header field.
scr_cash_viewing_an_ach_bank_configurati.ifSkipped: Rejections take longer to diagnose and vendor payments are delayed.
redFlags: Configuration differs from bank's current spec

scr_cash_deleting_an_ach_bank_configurat.purpose: Deletes an ACH origination configuration for a bank the company no longer uses, for example after all property accounts moved to a new treasury bank.
scr_cash_deleting_an_ach_bank_configurat.outcome: Obsolete origination settings cannot be selected for payment files.
scr_cash_deleting_an_ach_bank_configurat.rootCause: Leaving configurations for closed relationships risks generating files to the wrong bank.
scr_cash_deleting_an_ach_bank_configurat.ifSkipped: Files may be generated with obsolete settings and rejected.
redFlags: Deleting configurations still linked to active accounts

scr_cash_ach_bank_configuration_page.purpose: The page for entering ACH origination details — company name and ID, originating bank routing, file format options.
scr_cash_ach_bank_configuration_page.outcome: A complete ACH origination profile for a bank.
scr_cash_ach_bank_configuration_page.rootCause: Each field maps to NACHA file headers; errors cause rejections or misrouted files.
scr_cash_ach_bank_configuration_page.ifSkipped: Files cannot be generated or are rejected.

scr_cash_electronic_payment_bank_configu.purpose: Lists electronic payment bank configurations — settings for non-ACH electronic payment services (e.g., virtual card or payment service providers) by bank.
scr_cash_electronic_payment_bank_configu.outcome: Each electronic payment channel is configured per bank.
scr_cash_electronic_payment_bank_configu.rootCause: Companies use multiple electronic payment channels; each requires its own configuration to generate files correctly.
scr_cash_electronic_payment_bank_configu.ifSkipped: Electronic payments through those channels fail.

scr_cash_adding_an_electronic_payment_ba.purpose: Adds an electronic payment bank configuration so a bank account can issue payments through that channel.
scr_cash_adding_an_electronic_payment_ba.outcome: A new electronic payment channel is available for vendor payments.
scr_cash_adding_an_electronic_payment_ba.rootCause: New payment channels (e.g., virtual card programs that earn rebates) require setup before use.
scr_cash_adding_an_electronic_payment_ba.ifSkipped: Channel cannot be used, forgoing efficiencies or rebates.
redFlags: Configurations not tested before live use

scr_cash_editing_an_electronic_bank_paym.purpose: Edits an electronic payment configuration when provider or bank settings change.
scr_cash_editing_an_electronic_bank_paym.outcome: Electronic payments continue after provider changes.
scr_cash_editing_an_electronic_bank_paym.rootCause: Provider specification changes break file generation unless configurations are updated.
scr_cash_editing_an_electronic_bank_paym.ifSkipped: Payments through that channel fail after the provider changes its specification.

scr_cash_viewing_an_electronic_payment_b.purpose: Views an electronic payment bank configuration — provider identifiers, originating account and file settings — to verify it or to diagnose a failed payment batch.
scr_cash_viewing_an_electronic_payment_b.outcome: Configuration can be checked quickly when a batch of electronic payments fails.
scr_cash_viewing_an_electronic_payment_b.rootCause: Failed electronic payment batches usually trace to configuration mismatches with the provider; viewing the settings is the first diagnostic step before contacting the provider.
scr_cash_viewing_an_electronic_payment_b.ifSkipped: Failures take longer to diagnose and vendor payments are delayed.

scr_cash_deleting_an_electronic_payment_.purpose: Deletes an electronic payment configuration for a payment channel or provider that is no longer used.
scr_cash_deleting_an_electronic_payment_.outcome: Obsolete channels cannot be selected for payments.
scr_cash_deleting_an_electronic_payment_.rootCause: Removing unused channels prevents payments being routed through a discontinued provider.
scr_cash_deleting_an_electronic_payment_.ifSkipped: Payments may be routed to an inactive channel and fail.

scr_cash_electronic_payment_bank_configu.purpose: The page for entering an electronic payment channel's settings for a bank — provider IDs, originating account and file options — before payments can be sent through it.
scr_cash_electronic_payment_bank_configu.outcome: A complete configuration for the channel.
scr_cash_electronic_payment_bank_configu.rootCause: Complete, accurate settings are required for the provider to accept payment files; a single wrong identifier rejects the whole batch.
scr_cash_electronic_payment_bank_configu.ifSkipped: Files are rejected by the provider and vendors go unpaid.
